chunks: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amer narrated to us, from his uncle 'Abdullah ibn 'Amer, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Ziyad al-Karkhi, who said: I heard Abu 'Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) say:

If an enemy of Ali were to come to the Euphrates while it is flowing in abundance, its water overflowing over its two banks, and he took a drink from it and said 'In the name of God,' and when he drank it he said 'Praise be to God,' that would be nothing but carrion, or blood poured forth, or the flesh of swine.

key_terms.الفرات: The Euphrates -- one of the great rivers of Iraq, symbolizing abundance and purity
key_terms.دم مسفوح: Blood poured forth -- flowing blood, one of the prohibited items in Islamic dietary law
key_terms.عدو علي: Enemy of Ali -- one who harbors enmity toward Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS)
key_terms.لحم خنزير: Flesh of swine -- pork, categorically forbidden in Islamic law
key_terms.ميتة: Carrion -- dead animal not slaughtered according to Islamic law; ritually impure

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about enemies of Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) teaches that enmity toward Imam Ali (AS) renders even the most blessed actions spiritually void. Using imagery from Quran 6:145 -- which lists the three categories of prohibited food (carrion, blood, swine) -- the Imam declares that for one who harbors hatred of Ali, even drinking pure water from the abundant Euphrates while invoking God's name amounts to consuming what is forbidden. This hadith was narrated in the context of Shia devotional gatherings and underscores the centrality of wilayah (loyalty to the Ahl al-Bayt) in the Shia understanding of spiritual acceptance of deeds.
